systems.name: Bay Bridge Railway
systems.notes: The state-owned railway on the Bay Bridge's lower deck, with the Transbay Terminal loop and the East Bay yards, 1939–1958. The Key System, the Interurban Electric Railway and the Sacramento Northern ran their trains over it.

systems.name: California Pacific Railroad
systems.notes: From the ferry at South Vallejo to Sacramento (1868-69), with the Napa Valley Railroad (1865-68) as its branch from Napa Junction to Calistoga; part of the Central Pacific's system from 1871 and leased to it from 1876.

systems.name: California Street Cable Railroad
systems.notes: Leland Stanford's company, 1878; bought by the city in 1952.

systems.name: Central Pacific Railroad
systems.notes: The Pacific Railroad's western end: the 1869 line into Oakland, and its Northern Railway along the bay shore to Martinez (1876-78) and by the Benicia train ferry to Suisun (1879). Leased to the Southern Pacific Company from 1885.

systems.name: Clay Street Hill Railroad
systems.notes: Andrew Hallidie's first cable railway, 1873.

systems.name: East Bay streetcars (Oakland Traction and its successors)
systems.notes: The local streetcar lines of Oakland, Berkeley, Alameda and Richmond, run by the Oakland Traction Company, then East Bay Street Railways (from 1930), East Bay Transit (from 1936) and Key System (from the 1940s), until the last cars of 1948. Each line lists the operator its orders name.

systems.name: Ferries & Cliff House Railway
systems.notes: Also called the Powell Street Railway (Callwell p. 12).

systems.name: Golden Gate Ferries
systems.notes: The auto ferries from Hyde Street, 1922–1938: Golden Gate Ferries, Ltd., then from 1929 Southern Pacific-Golden Gate Ferries, Ltd. Not today's Golden Gate Ferry.

systems.name: Interurban Electric Railway
systems.notes: The Southern Pacific subsidiary that ran the East Bay electric lines in their last years.

systems.name: Key System
systems.notes: The Key Route trains and ferries, from 1903, under several corporate names; each line lists its operators by date.

systems.name: Market Street Railway and United Railroads
Martinez–Benicia ferry
systems.notes: Auto ferries across the Carquinez Strait, 1913-1962.

systems.name: Mt. Tamalpais & Muir Woods Railway
systems.notes: Built as the Mill Valley & Mount Tamalpais Scenic Railway (1896), "the crookedest railroad in the world", from Mill Valley to the summit of Mount Tamalpais, with a branch to Muir Woods from 1906 or 1907; the Mt. Tamalpais & Muir Woods Railway from 1913.

systems.name: North Pacific Coast Railroad
systems.notes: A narrow-gauge railroad from the ferry at Sausalito by San Anselmo, White's Hill, Point Reyes and Tomales to the Russian River (1875-77) and Cazadero (1886). Its successors, the North Shore Railroad and the Northwestern Pacific, electrified the Sausalito-San Anselmo end in 1903 and ran the rest by steam until 1930-33.

systems.name: Northwestern Pacific Railroad
systems.notes: Here, its third-rail electric lines in southern Marin, built by the North Shore Railroad and opened in 1903.

systems.name: Petaluma & Santa Rosa Railway
systems.notes: An electric interurban from the steamer landing at Petaluma to Sebastopol, where it divided for Santa Rosa and for Graton and Forestville (1904-05), with a branch from Liberty to Two Rock (1913). Its passenger cars ran until July 1, 1932; freight went on.

systems.name: Petaluma Street Railroad
systems.notes: Petaluma's one horsecar line (incorporated 1889), from the car barn at 12th and F Sts across the town and Petaluma Creek to the fairgrounds; bought by the Petaluma & Santa Rosa in 1903 for its franchise, and never electrified.

systems.name: Richmond and San Rafael Ferry and Transportation Co.
Sacramento Northern Railway
systems.notes: Built from Oakland as the Oakland & Antioch and the Oakland, Antioch & Eastern (1911-13), then the San Francisco-Sacramento Railroad, and from 1929 the Sacramento Northern. Here, its line from Oakland to Bay Point.

systems.name: Atchison, Topeka and Santa Fe Railway
systems.notes: Its line from Stockton by Antioch and Pinole to Richmond, built as the San Francisco & San Joaquin Valley Railway (1900), with its own ferry from Ferry Point at Point Richmond to the foot of Market St until 1933. Today's BNSF line; the Gold Runner runs on it from Bay Point east.

systems.name: Santa Rosa Street Railways
systems.notes: Santa Rosa's horsecar lines: the Santa Rosa City Railroad on Fourth St and McDonald Ave (1877), the South Side, later Union, Street Railway to the race track (1888) and the Central Street Railway on Humboldt St (1892), all under one owner from 1897 and called the Santa Rosa Street Railways from 1902. None was electrified; only the first is drawn.

systems.name: San Francisco and North Pacific Railroad
systems.notes: Peter Donahue's railroad from the steamer landing at Donahue by Petaluma to Santa Rosa (1870) and Cloverdale (1872), with a branch from San Rafael (1879) and a line to the ferry at Point Tiburon (1885); part of the Northwestern Pacific from 1907. SMART runs on much of its track.

systems.name: South Pacific Coast Railway
systems.notes: A narrow-gauge railroad from Alameda by Newark and San José to Los Gatos (1878) and over the Santa Cruz Mountains to Santa Cruz (1880), leased to the Southern Pacific from 1887.

systems.name: Southern Pacific Company
systems.notes: Here, its East Bay electric lines (the Red Trains), electrified from 1911.

systems.name: San Francisco-Vallejo ferry
systems.notes: The Hatch brothers' ferry of 1895, the Monticello Steamship Co.'s from 1904, then the Golden Gate Ferry Co.'s and from 1929 Southern Pacific Golden Gate Ferries'.
